messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I’m seeing ~12 PRs fail the SAST job `static-scan` in the last 3 hours, all from the same dependency bump series.
sec-bot: automated alert: nightly-scan failure detected for project/redwood-core — https://ci.redwood/internal/job/3123 (SAST)
Maria: Can you paste the failing snippet from the job logs?
Alex: ```
2026-03-22T18:12:04Z ERROR KMSAccessDenied: failed to decrypt artifact-key for scanner-service-account@redwood.iam: PermissionDenied
at kms/crypto.Decrypt (service: cloudkms.googleapis.com)
```
Jonah: That looks like the scanner SA lost the decrypt role. Likely an IAM drift after the infra change last week. It needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter (or equivalent).
Priya: Audit logs show a denied request at 2026-03-22T18:11:58Z — principal: serviceAccount:scanner-service-account@redwood.iam. I can forward the exact log entry. We should preserve that log for compliance (export to BigQuery).
Alex: Confirmed — same principal in all failing runs. Aside from the immediate fix, we should decide ownership for multi-PR scan noise — it's noisy for app teams. Thoughts on centralizing triage?
Maria: Proposal: route all scan failures for infra/* & deps/* to #security-scans automatically, and add a `scan-owner` label (security-team or repo-team). For cross-PR dependency bumps, assign a single owner to coordinate triage.
Jonah: I can implement a small GitLab webhook that watches the SAST job status and auto-creates an issue with the scan log + suggested owner based on CODEOWNERS. It can also attach the KMS audit log snippet.
Priya: For the immediate permission issue: two options — (1) restore the SA IAM binding to the KMS key with minimal role and record the change in the audit log, or (2) implement an ephemeral grant flow for CI to request decrypt role with TTL=10m. Option 2 is cleaner but requires infra work. Compliance prefers explicit audit entries either way.
Alex: For short-term unblock, please do (1) with an explicit changelog entry. For medium term, Jonah + Priya, can you pair on (2) and the webhook?
Maria: Runbook sketch: 1) identify failing runs -> gather job log + KMS deny entry -> restore minimal binding -> re-run SAST job -> mark issue with root cause + PR list -> if frequent, trigger rollback automation for the dep bump.
Jonah: I’ll draft the webhook and a small runbook doc. Sample command to rebind (GCP example):
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck \
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-service-account@redwood.iam \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Priya: Also capture the KMS key version and principal in the audit export: we need to keep key version metadata for at least 13 months per compliance. I’ll open a BigQuery export job and add the retention policy.
Alex: Thanks — I’ll file an infra ticket to restore the binding and link this thread. Can someone volunteer to update the security runbook doc after Jonah drafts it?
Maria: I’ll update the runbook once Jonah posts a draft. Assigning: Jonah -> webhook + runbook draft, Priya -> audit export + compliance check, Alex -> infra ticket + short-term bind. @sec-bot please annotate the ticket with the original CI failures. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: noted. Created internal incident INC-2026-041: linked PRs [#4321,#4323,#4330] and attached CI logs.
Alex: Great — follow-ups in the ticket. If anything weird shows up (different principal, or role already present), ping @oncall.
Maria: One more note — for future noisy dependency bumps we should consider letting SAST run but mark PR as "scan-warning" rather than hard-blocking until we tune the rules. Low false-positive waves cause churn.
Jonah: Agreed. We can add a decider bot that converts failures to warnings for the first X PRs in a short window and escalates if pattern persists.
Alex: OK — short-term fix first. Thanks all.
